cultures.name: Velani
cultures.description: Coastal and estuary farmers and fishers; children carry a patronymic.

cultures.name: Sukeru
cultures.description: River-valley cultivators; descent and names follow the mother.

cultures.name: Orvathi
cultures.description: Upland herders and miners organised in patrilineal clans.

cultures.name: Daethi
cultures.description: Grassland herders and cultivators who name people after their home settlement.

cultures.name: Ilunai
cultures.description: Forest-edge cultivators, foragers and woodworkers with matrilineal clans.

demography.description: Siler mortality (a1=0.48, b1=1.15, a2=0.0155, a3=0.0004, b3=0.085) giving e0 ≈ 24.6 years; Coale–Trussell natural fertility schedule; twin rate 1.2% and sex ratio at birth 1,050. All values are chosen defaults screened for plausibility, not fitted to data; disability prevalence is an uncalibrated default.

citations.citation: Coale, A. J., & Demeny, P. (1983). Regional Model Life Tables and Stable Populations (2nd ed.). Academic Press.
citations.usedFor: Range of pre-modern mortality levels (Model West levels 2–4) that the Siler parameters are chosen within.

citations.citation: Bagnall, R. S., & Frier, B. W. (1994). The Demography of Roman Egypt. Cambridge University Press.
citations.usedFor: Plausible ancient life expectancy, household size and household composition used to check the seed report.

citations.citation: Frier, B. W. (2000). Demography. In The Cambridge Ancient History, Vol. XI (2nd ed., pp. 787–816). Cambridge University Press.
citations.usedFor: Life expectancy at birth of roughly 20–30 years for the early Roman Empire.

citations.citation: Coale, A. J., & Trussell, T. J. (1974). Model fertility schedules. Population Index, 40(2), 185–258.
citations.usedFor: Natural marital fertility schedule n(a) by five-year age group, scaled by each culture's level M.

citations.citation: Hammel, E. A., & Laslett, P. (1974). Comparing household structure over time and between cultures. Comparative Studies in Society and History, 16(1), 73–109.
citations.usedFor: Household form categories (solitary, nuclear, extended/stem, multiple/joint).
